handbookNote: Grounded in the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (TWRA) boating safety program (tn.gov/twra), including TWRA's own Boating Education page, Watercraft Equipment Checklist, Boating Registration page, Non-Motorized Vessel (Paddlecraft) Permit page, Marine Sanitation Regulations, and Boat-Ed's Tennessee-specific course/law pages -- Tennessee's boater education mandate is genuine and independently confirmed by both TWRA's own official page and by two independent NASBLA-approved course vendors (Boat-Ed and BoatUS Foundation): Tennessee residents born after January 1, 1989 who operate a vessel with more than 8.5 horsepower must hold a TWRA Boating Safety Education Certificate, with an adult-supervision exemption (an adult 18+ born on or before the cutoff date aboard), and non-resident visitors able to satisfy the requirement with any NASBLA-approved certificate -- unlike most states in this project's boating rollout, Tennessee is more centralized than the typical 'many independent vendors' model: TWRA directly delegates and administers its own proctored online exam (reachable after purchasing a ~$13 Type 600 Boating Safety Exam Permit), which BoatUS Foundation's own Tennessee page explicitly confirms its free course does NOT satisfy, steering residents back to the TWRA-approved pathway or a separately-marketed, independently-TWRA-approved paid course (Boat-Ed's $54.95 Tennessee Boating Safety Course, which independently reports an 80% final-exam passing score with unlimited retake attempts and a separate 70% unit-quiz threshold, matching this project's WA/AZ/MA 80%/unlimited-attempts boating convention); the exact question count on TWRA's own delegated exam is not published on TWRA's site and is therefore left unconfirmed rather than asserted (a third, non-TWRA-satisfying vendor, BoatUS Foundation, separately advertises 60 final-exam questions on a course explicitly stated not to meet Tennessee's requirement, so that figure is not treated as confirming the TWRA-delegated exam's format) -- content also grounded in Tennessee's extensive TVA reservoir system (Norris, Cherokee, Percy Priest, Center Hill, Tims Ford, Douglas, Watauga, Kentucky Lake, Chickamauga, and other TVA lakes), which drives significant recreational boating and carries reservoir-specific hazards such as below-dam currents (Tennessee mandates a flotation device for ALL boaters below dams regardless of age), seasonal water-level fluctuation exposing submerged hazards, and TWRA's own explicit warnings against teak surfing, dragging, and skiing within 20 feet of a moving watercraft due to fatal carbon-monoxide exposure risk -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (PFDs, required equipment, Navigation Rules, aids to navigation, cold-water immersion, weather, and towing/water-sports safety); federal boating-accident-reporting deadlines (48 hours / 10 days) are presented as the general baseline since a Tennessee-specific deviation from that federal threshold was not independently re-verified against the exact state statute in this build -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
